newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends sharply higher on soybean gains.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends sharply higher on soybean gains.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures ended sharply higher on Friday, boosted by gains in soybeans tied to rumors China had purchased U.S. soybeans, traders said.

"The talk of the Chinese interest in the U.S. beans gave the funds a reason to reload long positions," said John Kleist, director of agricultural research for ING Futures and Options. "Half of it could be tied to fundementals and half of it to the technicals."
U.S. export sources said China appeared to have bought at least one cargo of U.S. soybeans and possibly two more on Thursday night.

But some exporters said the sale made little economic sense since Brazilian prices were below U.S. values. Still, some floor sources cited "reliability of supply", saying China needed prompt shipment and could not wait for Brazilian soybeans which have been delayed several times this year.
Soymeal ended $8.60 to $0.60 per ton higher with May up $8.60 at $281.60. Soyoil closed 0.22 to 0.09 cent per lb higher with May up 0.12 at 24.97.
Chartists said technical indicators for soymeal had turned bullish which attracted fund buying interest. Pit sources said Refco Inc bought at least 1,300 lots of soymeal.
